sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR status >= 500)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-07-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-08-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump), 3) AS p_problem, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump) >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 5, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

46 log lines matched 'rts panic! - stopping execution' across 38 distinct nodes, first at 2005-10-01 11:02:59 and last at 2005-10-31 20:44:07.

The ciod daemon on BGL I/O nodes lost its CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116 ("Link has been severed"). The new pattern 968 first appeared at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 on node R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, and that node's immediately preceding line was "ciod: Received signal 15".
Scope: Dataset bgl. Day window 2005-11-17 00:00:00 → 2005-11-18 00:00:00, plus a corpus-wide first/last check for pattern 968. Baseline is 2005-11-10 05:00:00 → 2005-11-17 05:00:00. Search and context row lists are truncated to a few rows; counts are full totals. Text matches overall: 49651 log lines.
Pattern 968 first appeared at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 on node R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11 (line_id 4215995, APP, FATAL): "ciod: Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:43572, Link has been severed".
On 2005-11-17 the matching lines ran from 05:33:24.623263 to 06:17:09.268580: 1008 log lines on 504 distinct nodes. The top nodes shown have 2 log lines each (the U01 and U11 I/O nodes of each node card).
Just before the first error, the same node logged at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.491562 (KERNEL, INFO): "ciod: Received signal 15, code=0, errno=0, address=0x000001b0". It was the only earlier line on that node in the hour before.
The same sequence repeats on other nodes. R77-M0-N4-I:J18-U11 logged "ciod: Received signal 15..." at 05:33:24.852317, then "...Link has been severed" at 05:33:24.982940. R77-M1-NC-I:J18-U01 and R77-M1-N8-I:J18-U11 behave the same way. Some later nodes show only the error line in the truncated sample.
The wider 05:18:24 → 05:33:34 window has 472 log lines before the first error (truncated to 30 shown). The 30 shown are KERNEL INFO torus lines from R63-M0-* compute-side nodes, e.g. "1 torus receiver x- input pipe error(s) (dcr 0x02ed) detected and corrected over 43 seconds" and "4167003 torus sender x- retransmission error(s) (dcr 0x02f5) detected and corrected over 76 seconds". They come from different nodes than the ciod errors.
Against the 7 days before (84 windows of 2 h), pattern 968 had baseline_lines 0, a max of 0 per window, and was new in the baseline. The 05:00–07:00 window had 1008 log lines, a rate of 504.0 per hour.
Pattern 968 continued after its first appearance. It has 26546 log lines on 1024 distinct nodes, with the last at 2006-01-03 11:56:38.877831.
The wider text match for the same message family goes back to 2005-07-20 11:54:27.005995, with other wording and other patterns, e.g. pattern 435 (after LOGIN_MESSAGE) and pattern 478 (after LOAD_MESSAGE). Pattern 968 itself first appears at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263.
Hypothesis: The ciod processes on the I/O nodes were terminated (signal 15) by a job kill, restart or control-system action, which closed their CioStream connections to 172.16.96.116 and produced the 'Link has been severed' errors. The torus retransmission lines on R63 may be unrelated background noise. Would confirm: Check whether 'Received signal 15' (pattern 960) precedes the error on every one of the 504 nodes. facts.statement: Pattern 968 first appeared at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 on node R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11 (line_id 4215995, APP, FATAL): "ciod: Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:43572, Link has been severed".

Just before the first error, the same node logged at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.491562 (KERNEL, INFO): "ciod: Received signal 15, code=0, errno=0, address=0x000001b0". It was the only earlier line on that node in the hour before.

The same sequence repeats on other nodes. R77-M0-N4-I:J18-U11 logged "ciod: Received signal 15..." at 05:33:24.852317, then "...Link has been severed" at 05:33:24.982940. sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR status >= 500)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-04 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump), 3) AS p_problem, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump) >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 5, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump), 3) AS p_problem, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_fault * (1 - Block freed." at 44 bursts against 29 in the previous period (+15). Machine check, uncorrectable/parity error and Microloader patterns also rose. The list is truncated, so other growers may exist.
Scope: Dataset bgl, October 2005 (2005-10-01 00:00 to 2005-11-01 00:00), compared with the previous period 2005-08-31 00:00 to 2005-10-01 00:00 (slightly longer than September). Filter: problem patterns only (fault probability x (1 - dump probability) >= 0.5), ownership by component. Results are TRUNCATED: 84 candidate patterns, of which the growth ranking shows 15 and the burst ranking shows 10. The team weekly trend covers 2005-09-01 to 2005-11-01 and is not truncated.
Pattern 261 'Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed.' (KERNEL, node-platform, FATAL) had 44 bursts in October against 29 in the previous period, a change of 15. It had 47 log lines and was active in 6 weeks. The recorded node count is 0.
Pattern 93 'machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error' (KERNEL, node-platform) had 10 bursts against 5 previously, a change of 5. It affected 8 nodes over 5 weeks active, with 10 log lines.
Eleven KERNEL patterns (ids 120, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 135, 153, 154, 158, 160: uncorrectable/parity/DDR errors) each had 4 bursts against 2 previously, a change of 2. Each affected 4 nodes over 4 weeks active, with a top-node share of 0.25. All are owned by node-platform and were first seen on 2005-06-08.
Pattern 467 'Microloader Assertion' (KERNEL, node-platform, FATAL) had 2 bursts against 0 previously. It had 18 log lines on 18 nodes over 2 weeks active.
Pattern 318 'NodeCard is not fully functional' (HARDWARE, node-platform) had 3 bursts against 1 previously, a change of 2. It was on 1 node (top-node share 1.0) with 5 log lines.
Patterns that went down in the burst ranking: pattern 69 'rts panic! - stopping execution' (node-platform) had 33 bursts against 51 (change -18). Pattern 33 'machine check interrupt' (node-platform) had 34 against 38 (change -4). Pattern 166 'Can not get assembly information for node card' (cluster-control) had 20 against 23 (change -3). Pattern 478 'ciod: Error reading message prefix...' (hpc-workloads) had 8 against 14 (change -6).
node-platform weekly log lines were 21676 (week of 2005-10-03), 25677 (10-10), 33923 (10-17), 20471 (10-24) and 9168 (10-31), against 18052 in the week of 2005-09-26. The week starting 10-31 covers only the last day of the period.
In October node-platform produced 112809 of 153351 log lines. hpc-workloads produced 36295 and cluster-control 4247.
1. Investigate first: 'Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed.' (FATAL job timeouts) keeps recurring and has the largest increase. — owner node-platform — 44 bursts vs 29 previously (change 15), 47 log lines, 6 weeks active. This is the highest burst count and the largest absolute increase in both rankings. — Node-platform should check whether the timeouts cluster on particular blocks, midplanes or times. They should also check why the node field is empty (nodes = 0) for this pattern.
2. Machine check interrupt: L<N> major internal error (hardware failure) recurring more often across many nodes. — owner node-platform — 10 bursts vs 5 previously (change 5), 8 nodes, 5 weeks active, top-node share 0.2. — Check the 8 affected nodes and their locations for a shared hardware or rack cause.
3. Group of 11 uncorrectable/parity/DDR memory-error patterns that all doubled together. — owner node-platform — Each: 4 bursts vs 2 previously (change 2), 4 nodes, 4 weeks active, top-node share 0.25. — Check whether the patterns share the same 4 nodes and timestamps, and treat them as one memory-fault event rather than 11 separate problems.
4. Microloader Assertion appeared in October bursts after none in the previous period. — owner node-platform — 2 bursts vs 0 previously, 18 nodes, 18 log lines, 2 weeks active. — Check whether the 18 nodes share a boot or microloader image or a restart event.
5. NodeCard is not fully functional recurring, concentrated on a single node. — owner node-platform — 3 bursts vs 1 previously (change 2), 1 node, 5 log lines. — Inspect the single node card involved.
Hypothesis: The job-kill timeouts (pattern 261) may be a downstream symptom of the node hardware and machine-check errors rising over the same period. Would confirm: Correlate timestamps and blocks of pattern 261 bursts with bursts of patterns 93, 33 and the memory-error group. Overlap would support it; no overlap would rule it out.
Hypothesis: The 11 memory-error patterns with identical counts (4 bursts, 4 nodes, top-node share 0.25) may be one shared hardware event logged under many templates. Would confirm: Compare the node IDs and burst start times across these patterns in the raw log lines.
Unknown: Root cause of any of these patterns is not established by the logs.
Unknown: Customer impact, downtime and cost are not in the logs.
Unknown: The comparison period is 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01, not exactly September.
Unknown: Results are truncated (84 candidates, only the top 15 by growth and top 10 by bursts shown), so other worsening patterns, including ones owned by other teams, may exist.
Unknown: The node count for pattern 261 is recorded as 0, so its spread across nodes is unknown.

Next step: Run the growth ranking again with a higher limit (84 candidates) to see whether hpc-workloads or cluster-control patterns also grew. — The current growth list is truncated at 15 of 84 and shows only node-platform patterns as growing.
Next step: Review the 8 nodes behind pattern 93 and the 4 nodes behind the memory-error group for shared hardware. — Both groups recurred across multiple weeks (5 and 4) and at least doubled their bursts or grew by 5.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR status >= 500)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-04 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR status >= 500)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-07-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-08-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump), 3) AS p_problem, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump) >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 5, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

Not one bad node: 'rts panic! - stopping execution' hit 38 distinct nodes in October 2005 (46 log lines), and no node had more than 2 log lines. It is spread across many nodes and owned by node-platform, but these logs do not show whether that amounts to the whole fleet.
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01 (previous period 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01). Filters: text search 'rts panic stopping execution', pattern 69, component KERNEL for the ranking. The sample search and the per-node count were truncated at their limits (5 sample rows, top 10 nodes); the totals, the weekly trend and the KERNEL pattern ranking were not truncated.
The search matched 46 log lines on 38 distinct nodes, first at 2005-10-01 11:02:59.249894 and last at 2005-10-31 20:44:07.437222.
In the per-node count, the highest count was 2 log lines per node (for example R02-M1-N6-C:J12-U01 and R62-M0-N4-C:J13-U01); 38 nodes in total.
Pattern 69 (rts panic! - stopping execution) has top_node_share 0.043, 33 bursts in the period vs 51 in the previous period (change -18), and was active in 6 weeks.
All 46 log lines belong to one team, node-platform.
Weekly log lines by week start: 2005-09-26: 6, 2005-10-03: 4, 2005-10-10: 2, 2005-10-17: 23, 2005-10-24: 8, 2005-10-31: 3.
Two panics on different nodes, R22-M0-NA-C:J11-U01 and R21-M0-NB-C:J07-U01, occurred at 2005-10-02 09:10:45.032440 and 2005-10-02 09:10:49.173762.
1. rts panic! - stopping execution: a recurring kernel panic that is spread across many nodes, not tied to one node. Investigate first. — owner node-platform — 46 log lines, 38 nodes, 33 bursts vs 51 previously (change -18), 6 weeks active, top_node_share 0.043; 23 of the 46 log lines fall in the week starting 2005-10-17. — Treat as a shared cause rather than a node swap. Correlate the week of 2005-10-17 panics and the 2005-10-02 09:10 pair with jobs, firmware or software changes at those times.
2. machine check interrupt: another fatal kernel pattern with similar node spread. — owner node-platform — 37 log lines, 34 nodes, 34 bursts vs 38 previously (change -4), 6 weeks active, top_node_share 0.081. — Check whether it co-occurs with the rts panics on the same nodes or in the same time windows.
3. Kill job timed out. Block freed.: the most frequent fatal kernel pattern by bursts, and rising. — owner node-platform — 47 log lines, 44 bursts vs 29 previously (change 15), 6 weeks active; the nodes field shows 0 in the results. — Confirm why no node is recorded and whether the rise is linked to the panic activity.
Hypothesis: A shared trigger (for example a job, software or firmware change) may explain the panics landing on many nodes at similar times, such as the week starting 2005-10-17. Would confirm: Compare panic timestamps and nodes with the job or allocation records and with other fatal patterns on the same nodes; a common job or block would support it.
Hypothesis: Unrelated per-node faults may each cause an occasional panic, giving a low per-node count. Would confirm: Check whether the panicking nodes show hardware error patterns (machine check, parity) near the panic time, and whether panics recur after those nodes are reset.
Unknown: The root cause of the panic is not established by these logs.
Unknown: The logs show no job, hardware or customer impact, downtime or cost.
Unknown: Whether the panics were fixed by a reset or reboot is not shown.
Unknown: Per-node counts come from a truncated top-10 list; the other 28 nodes were not listed.
Next step: Pull the 23 log lines from the week starting 2005-10-17 and group them by rack, midplane and minute, and join with job allocation data. — 23 of 46 log lines fall in that week, and spread across 38 nodes points toward a shared cause.
Next step: List all 38 nodes and check each for earlier or later fatal patterns, including machine check interrupt. — The per-node count was truncated at 10, and the machine check interrupt pattern has a similar node spread (34 nodes).
Next step: Check why 'Kill job timed out. Block freed.' has no node recorded and whether its rise (change 15) is related. — It has the most bursts among fatal KERNEL patterns (44) and its nodes value is 0.

D-E05|ours|1.text:
The ciod daemon on BGL I/O nodes logged FATAL 'Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:…, Link has been severed' (pattern 968). It started at 05:33:24.623263 on R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11. On that node, 'ciod: Received signal 15' was logged just before the error, and the same pairing appears on other nodes in the first seconds.
Scope: Dataset bgl. Main window 2005-11-17 00:00:00 → 2005-11-18 00:00:00, plus a 2005-11-17 05:03:24 → 05:34:24 context window, a 2005-11-17 05:00 → 07:00 rate check against 2005-11-10 05:00 → 2005-11-17 05:00, and a whole-corpus search. The text query is 'ciod Error reading message prefix Link has been severed' and the rate check is filtered to pattern_id 968. Row listings are truncated (searches show 10 or 3 rows, context shows 30 lines per side); totals and counts are complete.
On 2005-11-17 the query matched 1008 log lines on 504 distinct nodes, first at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 and last at 2005-11-17 06:17:09.268580.
The first matching line is line_id 4215995, component APP, severity FATAL, node R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, pattern_id 968: 'ciod: Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:43572, Link has been severed'.
Immediately before it, on the same node R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11 at 05:33:24.491562, the log has KERNEL INFO (pattern 960): 'ciod: Received signal 15, code=0, errno=0, address=0x000001b0'.
The same two-line sequence follows on other I/O nodes. R77-M0-N4-I:J18-U11 logs 'Received signal 15' at 05:33:24.852317 and the FATAL 'Link has been severed' line at 05:33:24.982940. R77-M1-NC-I:J18-U01 logs the signal at 05:33:25.183395 and the FATAL line at 05:33:25.311353.
Before the first error, the context window is dominated by KERNEL INFO torus messages from node R63-M0-ND-C:J16-U01 and other R63 nodes, e.g. at 05:33:24.287417: '4167003 torus sender x- retransmission error(s) (dcr 0x02f5) detected and corrected over 76 seconds'. These are on different nodes (R63 compute-side) and are marked 'detected and corrected'.
The failure spreads across many racks within seconds. Nodes in R77, R40, R41, R54 and R56 log the error between 05:33:24 and 05:33:29. The top-10 nodes listed each have 2 log lines (the -U01 and -U11 chips), across 504 nodes in total.
This pattern (968) is new relative to the prior week. The 2-hour window 2005-11-17 05:00 → 07:00 has 1008 log lines (504.0 per hour). The 84 earlier same-length windows from 2005-11-10 05:00 → 2005-11-17 05:00 have 0 baseline lines, and new_in_baseline is true.
A broader search of the same message family over the whole corpus gives 49651 matches on 1024 distinct nodes, from 2005-07-20 11:54:27.005995 to 2006-01-03 11:56:38.877831. The earliest rows are a different pattern (435) with a different wording: 'ciod: Error reading message prefix after LOGIN_MESSAGE on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:56214: Link has been severed'.
Hypothesis: ciod on each I/O node may have been terminated by signal 15 (SIGTERM), for example a job or partition kill or a control-system restart. Its CioStream connection to 172.16.96.116 would then have dropped, and ciod would have logged 'Link has been severed' as a consequence rather than as the root fault. Would confirm: Check whether every one of the 504 nodes has a 'Received signal 15' line shortly before its error line. Look at logs from the host at 172.16.96.116 (the service/control side) and any job, block-free or reboot events around 2005-11-17 05:33. Confirmation would be signal lines on all nodes and a matching control-side action. A lack of signal lines on some nodes would weaken it.
Unknown: What sent signal 15 and why: the logs shown do not identify the sender or root cause.
Unknown: Whether the R63 torus retransmission messages are related to the failure: they are on different nodes and are logged as corrected.
Unknown: What happened after 06:17:09.268580 and whether the nodes recovered: the ledger has no later lines for these nodes.
Unknown: Job, customer or cost impact is not in these logs.
Next step: Run a count_by node for pattern 960 ('ciod: Received signal 15') between 2005-11-17 05:03:24.623263 and 2005-11-17 06:17:09.268580 and compare it with the 504 nodes in pattern 968. Then run get_context on the last pattern-968 line (last_ts 2005-11-17 06:17:09.268580) to see what follows. — Tests whether signal 15 precedes the error on every one of the 504 nodes (ev-686abe1306), and shows how the burst ends, which the context window starting 2005-11-17 05:03:24.623263 (ev-072f95d5c3) does not cover.
Next step: Search logs from or about 172.16.96.116 (service/control host) and any block/partition free or job-kill messages around 2005-11-17 05:33:20 → 05:33:30. — All errors name the socket to 172.16.96.116 and begin at 05:33:24.623263 on R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, so the peer side is the next place to look for the trigger.

sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, coalesce(latency_ms / 1000.0, CAST(nullif(regexp_extract(body, 'Took ([\d.]+) seconds', 1), '') AS DOUBLE)) AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM patterns WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND (strpos(template, 'Took <N> seconds') > 0 OR strpos(template, ' time: <N>') > 0))) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.instance_id, l.request_id, coalesce(l.latency_ms / 1000.0, CAST(nullif(regexp_extract(l.body, 'Took ([\d.]+) seconds', 1), '') AS DOUBLE)) AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT f.line_id, f.ts, f.pattern_id, f.instance_id, f.request_id, round(f.value_s, 3) AS value_s, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(f.value_s / t.med, 2) AS ratio, f.body FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold ORDER BY ratio DESC, f.ts LIMIT 30

Two FATAL KERNEL "kernel panic" log lines (pattern 576) hit two different nodes on R43-M0 at 2005-08-19 13:56:00. Nothing else was logged on rack R43 in the hour before or after. The pattern is recurring across the corpus, but this burst is far above its usual hourly rate.
Scope: All datasets for the midplane search (2005-08-19 13:40:00 → 14:15:00, midplane R43-M0); bgl rack R43 for the context (2005-08-19 12:56:00.280831 → 14:56:00.280831); pattern 576 history over the whole corpus (2005-08-15 → 2005-11-11); baseline 2005-08-12 13:00:00 → 2005-08-19 13:00:00. No results were truncated.
On R43-M0 between 2005-08-19 13:40:00 and 14:15:00 there were 2 matching log lines on 2 distinct nodes, first at 2005-08-19 13:56:00.280831 and last at 2005-08-19 13:56:00.628434.
Verbatim first line: line_id 3069219, 2005-08-19 13:56:00.280831, KERNEL, FATAL, node R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01, pattern 576, body "kernel panic".
Verbatim second line: line_id 3069220, 2005-08-19 13:56:00.628434, KERNEL, FATAL, node R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11, pattern 576, body "kernel panic".
Before: bgl rack R43 had 0 log lines in the hour before the first panic (before_total 0). After: the only later log line in the hour after was the second panic (after_total 1).

cluster-control: 10 problem patterns, 44 bursts (previous period 64, change -20), 70389 log lines; top item score 68.4.

2. 'rts panic! - stopping execution' (system software failure) — owner node-platform — 49 bursts vs 24 in the previous period (change 25); 279 nodes; active in 5 weeks; score 96.0 — Prioritise ownership of a root-cause review; it is the most frequent and persistent top item.

Hypothesis: The Lustre mount failures (rank 1) and the ciod link-severed errors (rank 3) may share an underlying I/O or network cause. Would confirm: Check whether the two patterns' bursts overlap in time and nodes.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR status >= 500)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-29 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-06-04 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump), 3) AS p_problem, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_fault * (1 - In bgl, the recurring problems that rose in October 2005 versus the previous period are all owned by node-platform. The largest rise is "Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed.", at 44 bursts against 29. No worsening pattern was found for cluster-control or hpc-workloads in the top-15 growth list.
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01, compared with the tool's previous period 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01 (the tool's "September" window starts on 2005-08-31). Filters: problem patterns only (fault probability judgment), ranked by change in bursts. The growth list is truncated: 15 of 84 matching patterns are shown, so more patterns with the same +2 change may exist. The openstack dataset returned no matches (0).
"Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed." (KERNEL, FATAL, node-platform) had 44 bursts in the period against 29 in the previous period (change 15), across 47 log lines and 6 weeks active.
"machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error" (node-platform) had 10 bursts against 5 (change 5), on 8 nodes, 5 weeks active, 10 log lines.
Several KERNEL hardware or memory error patterns owned by node-platform (ids 120, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 135, 153, 154, 158, 160) each had 4 bursts against 2 (change 2), on 4 nodes and 4 weeks active.
"NodeCard is not fully functional" (HARDWARE, SEVERE, node-platform) had 3 bursts against 1 (change 2), on 1 node and 1 week active; top_node_share is 1.0.
"Microloader Assertion" (KERNEL, FATAL, node-platform) had 2 bursts against 0 (change 2), across 18 nodes and 2 weeks active.
Other top recurring problems did not worsen: "rts panic! - stopping execution" went from 51 to 33 bursts (change -18); "machine check interrupt" from 38 to 34 (change -4); "Can not get assembly information for node card" (cluster-control) from 23 to 20 (change -3); the ciod "Link has been severed" pattern (hpc-workloads) from 14 to 8 (change -6).
node-platform had 112809 of 153351 log lines in October, compared with 36295 for hpc-workloads and 4247 for cluster-control.
node-platform weekly log lines for weeks starting 2005-10-03, 10-10, 10-17, 10-24 and 10-31 were 21676, 25677, 33923, 20471 and 9168 (the 10-31 week is a partial week); the week starting 2005-09-26 had 18052.
1. Investigate first: "Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed." (FATAL kernel message, judged a job or application failure) recurs far more often than in the previous period. — owner node-platform — 44 bursts vs 29 previously (change 15), 47 log lines, 6 weeks active. This is the largest increase in the list and the pattern with the most bursts in October. — Check whether the timeouts cluster on particular jobs, blocks or time windows, and whether they accompany the machine-check patterns.
2. Machine check interrupt: L<N> major internal error (hardware failure) bursts doubled. — owner node-platform — 10 bursts vs 5 (change 5), 8 nodes, 5 weeks active, 10 log lines. — List the 8 affected nodes and check for repeat offenders or a shared hardware location.
3. A group of uncorrectable-error and parity-error kernel patterns (directory, EDRAM, DDR, read queue, memory manager; ids 120, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 135, 153, 154, 158, 160) each doubled. — owner node-platform — Each at 4 bursts vs 2 (change 2), 4 nodes, 4 weeks active. — Check whether the patterns fire together on the same 4 nodes (one underlying event) or independently.
4. "Microloader Assertion" is a pattern with no bursts in the previous period that appeared in 2 bursts in October. — owner node-platform — 2 bursts vs 0 (change 2), 18 nodes, 2 weeks active. — Check the dates and whether the 18 nodes share a software load or partition.
5. "NodeCard is not fully functional" bursts tripled but are concentrated on a single node. — owner node-platform — 3 bursts vs 1 (change 2), 1 node, 1 week active, top_node_share 1.0. — Check the state of that node card and whether it has been serviced.
Hypothesis: The rise in "Kill job timed out" bursts may be a symptom of node hardware faults (machine checks) rather than an independent job problem. Would confirm: Correlate timestamps and nodes of the kill-job bursts with machine-check and uncorrectable-error bursts; no overlap would rule it out.
Hypothesis: The identical 4-burst, 4-node, 4-week counts across many memory and parity patterns may mean they come from the same few events, so they may not be independent problems. Would confirm: Compare the node IDs and burst start times of patterns 120 to 160.
Unknown: Root cause of any of these increases is not established by the logs.
Unknown: Customer, job-loss, downtime or cost impact is not in the logs.
Unknown: The growth list is truncated (15 of 84 matches), so other patterns with the same change of 2 or smaller may not be shown.
Unknown: The nodes count for the kill-job pattern is 0, so its node spread cannot be determined from this result.
Unknown: The comparison window starts on 2005-08-31, not 2005-09-01, and is longer than the October period.
Next step: Pull node, timestamp and job/block details for the 44 "Kill job timed out" bursts and overlay them on the machine-check bursts. — It has the largest burst increase (44 vs 29) and could be linked to the hardware patterns.
Next step: List the 8 nodes behind the major internal error pattern and the 4 nodes behind the uncorrectable/parity pattern group; check hardware health. — Both rose (10 vs 5 and 4 vs 2 bursts) on a small number of nodes.
Next step: Re-run the growth ranking with a higher limit to see the patterns cut off by truncation (84 matches, 15 shown). — Several patterns tie at a change of 2, so the shown list may be incomplete.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR status >= 500)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-08-31 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-10-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump), 3) AS p_problem, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump) >= 0.5 ) SELECT *, count(*) OVER () AS candidates FROM base ORDER BY change DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id LIMIT 15

The first 'data TLB error interrupt' line in June 2005 was at 2005-06-05 00:08:13.410695 on node R20-M0-N2-C:J10-U11 (KERNEL, FATAL). It then spread to 466 nodes on 2005-06-05. After five days with no matches, one node, R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01, produced 152182 log lines on 2005-06-11.
Scope: All datasets (matches are bgl), 2005-06-01 to 2005-07-01, phrase search "data TLB error interrupt". Totals are 152659 log lines on 467 nodes. Sample rows were truncated (limit applied), but counts and the daily trend are complete. Matches were found only from 2005-06-05 to 2005-06-11.
There were 152659 matching log lines across 467 distinct nodes. The first was at 2005-06-05 00:08:13.410695 and the last at 2005-06-11 23:39:32.877740.
The first line was line_id 17742, component KERNEL, severity FATAL, on node R20-M0-N2-C:J10-U11, with the body "data TLB error interrupt".
Daily counts: 477 log lines on 2005-06-05, 0 on each day from 2005-06-06 to 2005-06-10, and 152182 on 2005-06-11.
The 2005-06-05 burst covered 477 log lines on 466 distinct nodes. The first was at 00:08:13.410695 and the last at 08:32:34.507576, on node R35-M0-N8-C:J11-U11. The busiest nodes had only 3 log lines each, for example R22-M0-N7-C:J04-U01.
The ten earliest log lines were all on R20 nodes (R20-M0-N2, R20-M0-ND, R20-M0-N9, R20-M1-N2, R20-M0-NE, R20-M0-N7) between 00:08:13.410695 and 00:08:23.880054, all FATAL.
The 2005-06-11 flood came from a single node, R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01, with 152182 log lines. They ran from 2005-06-11 17:17:44.898186 to 2005-06-11 23:39:32.877740, with distinct_nodes = 1 in that window.
Rate vs baseline: the 2005-06-11 window ran at 6340.917 log lines per hour, against a baseline of 2.839 per hour over the 7 prior days (477 baseline log lines). The ratio was 2233.3, and no baseline window reached 152182 (baseline_windows_at_or_above is 0).
Timeline at the start. Before, at 00:08:13.345847 on R20-M0-N2-C:J14-U11 (INFO): "generating core.3756". At, line 17742 at 00:08:13.410695 on R20-M0-N2-C:J10-U11 (FATAL): "data TLB error interrupt". After, at 00:08:13.433576 on R20-M0-N2-C:J06-U11 (INFO): "generating core.3758", and at 00:08:13.577322 on R20-M0-N2-C:J14-U01 (FATAL): "data TLB error interrupt".
In midplane R20-M0 there were 19 log lines in the 10 minutes before the first line and 492 in the 5 minutes after. The context shown is dominated by INFO "generating core.NNNN" lines (pattern_id 3), interleaved with the FATAL lines (pattern_id 31).
Hypothesis: The 2005-06-05 burst may be a job or partition-wide fault. Many compute chips in R20-M0 were writing core dumps at the same moment they reported TLB errors, and the pattern then appeared on 466 nodes. Would confirm: Check whether the nodes that logged the TLB error also logged 'generating core.*' within seconds, and whether they belong to the same job or partition. Check the job and RAS logs for 2005-06-05 00:08.
Hypothesis: The 2005-06-11 flood may be one faulty node, R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01, repeating the same interrupt in a loop, with no relation to the 2005-06-05 event. Would confirm: Look at the lines on that node just before 2005-06-11 17:17:44 and after 23:39:32, and check whether it was rebooted or replaced, or reported a hardware error.
Unknown: The root cause of either burst is not established by these logs.
Unknown: The logs do not show whether jobs failed or whether there was any customer impact or downtime.
Unknown: Whether the pattern occurred before 2005-06-01 is unknown, since the search was limited to June 2005.
Unknown: The 2005-06-11 count may be driven by log-rate repetition on one node rather than by distinct fault events.
Next step: Run get_context on dataset bgl, line_id 222716 (node R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01), using a window before the first line, and search that node for non-TLB lines before 2005-06-11 17:17:44.898186. — The flood started at 2005-06-11 17:17:44.898186 on a single node (ev-c2a1b7ca84), and the lines before it have not been inspected.
Next step: Query 'generating core' and 'data TLB error interrupt' together by node and minute for 2005-06-05 00:00 to 09:00, and map the 466 nodes to their racks and midplanes. — The burst began with core-dump lines on R20-M0-N2 and reached 466 nodes with 477 log lines.
Next step: Inspect node R30-M0-N9-C:J16-U01 (hardware, TLB or memory errors) and check the maintenance history. — It accounts for 152182 of the 152659 matching log lines.

Instance 9fafc51c-d0dd-41df-99e9-6c79d8334eaf was created, spawned and then deleted within about a minute. The logs show no WARNING or ERROR lines for it. nova-api accepted the create (202) and the delete (204), and nova-compute handled the claim, spawn, termination and cleanup.
Scope: Dataset openstack, 2017-05-16 22:51:36.968000 → 2017-05-16 22:52:20.587000. Filter: instance_id 9fafc51c-d0dd-41df-99e9-6c79d8334eaf, plus request-scoped context for req-3ac9b75e-aada-4a82-a102-140cc653fdaf and req-6dc007d0-d454-4226-977c-2e3431d1ad61. Results were not truncated.
25 log lines carry this instance_id, from 2017-05-16 22:51:36.968000 to 2017-05-16 22:52:20.587000. All of them are INFO from nova-compute. The node field is empty (distinct_nodes 0), so the host cannot be identified.
Before → create: nova-api logged at 22:51:36.647000: 10.11.10.1 "POST /v2/54fadb412c4e40cdbaed9335e4c35a9e/servers HTTP/1.1" status: 202 len: 733 time: 0.4779122 (latency_ms 477.9122). This is the same request_id as the first nova-compute line.

Spawn: "VM Started (Lifecycle Event)" at 22:51:51.023000 and "VM Paused (Lifecycle Event)" at 22:51:51.084000. "VM Resumed (Lifecycle Event)" appears twice, at 22:51:57.927000 and 22:51:58.055000. sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR status >= 500)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-07-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-08-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-08-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump), 3) AS p_problem, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump) >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 5, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

In October 2005 this is not one bad node: the 46 log lines of 'rts panic! - stopping execution' came from 38 distinct nodes, and no node in the top 10 had more than 2 lines. Whether that counts as fleet-wide cannot be judged from these logs, because the total fleet size is not in the ledger. The activity is clustered in time, with 14 log lines on 2005-10-23.
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-10-01 00:00:00 to 2005-11-01 00:00:00, full-text match on 'rts panic stopping execution'. The trend and the totals are complete. The node ranking shows only the top 10 of 38 nodes, and the line listing shows only 10 of 46 log lines. The top-patterns query was truncated (50 rows of 301 candidates) and did not list this pattern, so its bursts, weeks active and change vs the previous period are not available.
46 log lines matched, from 38 distinct nodes, between 2005-10-01 11:02:59.249894 and 2005-10-31 20:44:07.437222.

The 10 earliest matching log lines are all KERNEL, severity FATAL, pattern_id 69. Only R62-M0-N4-C:J13-U01 appears twice among them, at 2005-10-02 12:27:58.666393 and 2005-10-02 12:27:58.736534.
Daily counts are uneven: 14 log lines on 2005-10-23, 5 on 2005-10-02, 4 on 2005-10-19, and 0 on each day from 2005-10-05 to 2005-10-11.
For comparison, another fatal KERNEL pattern, 'rts: kernel terminated for reason <N>', had 1031 log lines on 1025 nodes with 2 bursts in the same period (3 in the previous period, change -1).

Bursts, weeks active and change vs the previous period are not in the ledger. — Check what ran around 2005-10-23, where the 14 log lines cluster, and whether the affected nodes share a rack, midplane or job.
2. 'rts: kernel terminated for reason <N>' (KERNEL, FATAL): a similar kernel-level fatal pattern that hit about a thousand nodes in only 2 bursts. Context for judging scale, not a confirmed link to the panic lines. — owner node-platform — 1031 log lines, 1025 nodes, 2 bursts vs 3 in the previous period (change -1), 2 weeks active. — Check whether its 2 bursts coincide with the days of the rts panic lines; if not, treat them as separate problems.
Hypothesis: The panics may follow a few job- or partition-level events, such as a bad program or kernel image on a set of nodes, rather than independent node faults, which would explain the clustering on 2005-10-23. Would confirm: Group the 46 log lines by timestamp, rack and midplane, and look for ciod or job lines from the same partitions at the same times. If they match, it is job-linked.
Hypothesis: The panic could be a symptom of unrelated hardware faults on different nodes, which would predict no time clustering and no shared rack. Would confirm: Compare the 38 nodes' hardware-failure patterns (for example, DISCOVERY events) in the same period.
Unknown: Total fleet size, so '38 nodes' cannot be turned into a fleet share from this ledger.

D-E05|ours|2.text:
The ciod daemons on BGL I/O nodes logged FATAL 'Error reading message prefix ... Link has been severed' (pattern 968). The first line is at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 on R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11. On that node it came right after 'ciod: Received signal 15', so the daemon was being signalled to terminate. The pattern spread to 504 nodes and was new compared with the previous 7 days.
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-11-17 00:00:00 → 2005-11-18 00:00:00 (rate check 2005-11-17 05:00:00 → 2005-11-17 06:00:00 vs 2005-11-10 05:00:00 → 2005-11-17 05:00:00). Filters: ciod message text and pattern_id 968, 967 and 960. Searches and context were truncated to row limits; the counts are totals.
On 2005-11-17 the message matched 1008 log lines on 504 distinct nodes, first at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263 and last at 2005-11-17 06:17:09.268580. Each of the 10 top nodes by count shows 2 lines.
The first line is component APP, severity FATAL, node R77-M0-NC-I:J18-U11, pattern_id 968: 'ciod: Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:43572, Link has been severed'.
Just before (05:33:24.491562), the same node logged KERNEL INFO 'ciod: Received signal 15, code=0, errno=0, address=0x000001b0'.
After the first line, the same signal 15 → severed pairing repeats on other nodes. For example, R77-M1-NC-I:J18-U01 logged signal 15 at 05:33:25.183395 and the severed line at 05:33:25.311353. Nodes in racks R77, R40, R41, R54 and R56 follow within seconds.
The latest 25 lines in the window 05:00:00 → 05:33:24 are KERNEL INFO torus messages from R63 nodes, e.g. 'R63-M0-ND-C:J14-U01 ... 1 torus receiver x- input pipe error(s) (dcr 0x02ed) detected and corrected over 43 seconds' at 05:33:23.885534. The last line before the first severed line, at 05:33:24.287417, is '4167003 torus sender x- retransmission error(s) (dcr 0x02f5) detected and corrected over 76 seconds'.
The torus sender retransmission pattern (967) first appears at 2005-11-17 05:33:06.707503 on R63-M0-N3-C:J15-U11, with 128 log lines on 64 nodes through 2005-11-17 06:14:56.354362.
The 'Received signal 15' pattern (960) first appears at 2005-11-17 05:14:17.105933 on R65-M0-N4-I:J18-U11, earlier than the first severed line at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263. It has 1072 log lines on 504 nodes, the last at 2005-11-17 06:17:14.969846.
Rate: pattern 968 has 504 log lines in 2005-11-17 05:00:00 → 2005-11-17 06:00:00 (504.0 per hour) against 0 baseline log lines (0.0 per hour) in the 168 earlier hourly windows, and new_in_baseline is true.
Across the whole corpus the broader message family matched 49651 log lines on 1024 nodes (first 2005-07-20 11:54:27.005995, last 2006-01-03 11:56:38.877831). Earlier variants are 'after LOGIN_MESSAGE' (pattern 435) and 'after LOAD_MESSAGE' (pattern 478).
The wording seen on 2005-11-17 is pattern 968, 'Error reading message prefix on CioStream socket to ..., Link has been severed', a different template from patterns 435 and 478.
Hypothesis: The ciod processes on the I/O nodes were terminated by SIGTERM (signal 15), for example a job or partition kill or a controlled restart. That closed their CioStream sockets to 172.16.96.116 and produced the 'Link has been severed' FATAL line. The R63 torus retransmission errors may be a separate or contributing hardware symptom. Would confirm: Check control-system or job-scheduler logs for a kill or partition free between 2005-11-17 05:14:17.105933 and 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263. Check whether every node with a severed line had a signal 15 line just before it. Check whether the R63 torus errors occur on nodes outside the affected set.
Unknown: The root cause and who or what sent signal 15 are not in these logs.
Unknown: Whether the 172.16.96.116 endpoint failed or was restarted is not shown.
Unknown: Whether the torus errors on R63 are related to the severed links is not established.
Unknown: Why signal 15 lines began earlier than the first severed line is not explained.
Unknown: Job, user or customer impact is not in the logs.
Next step: Run count_by node and a per-minute timeline for pattern_id 960 and pattern_id 968 over the span from the first pattern 960 line to the last pattern 968 line, and list nodes with 960 but no 968 after it. — Signal 15 starts at 2005-11-17 05:14:17.105933 and severed lines at 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263. This shows whether the two are paired on every node and how the earlier signal 15 lines relate to the severed lines.
Next step: Inspect logs of the service at 172.16.96.116 and the control system around 2005-11-17 05:14:17.105933 and 2005-11-17 05:33:24.623263, and search all components for the kill or restart request. — Every severed line points to a socket on 172.16.96.116, and the signal 15 source is not visible in these logs.
Next step: Query torus pattern 966 and 967 on R63 nodes from 2005-11-17 05:00:00 to 2005-11-17 06:00:00 and compare the node set with the severed-node set. — 967 starts at 2005-11-17 05:33:06.707503, shortly before the first severed line, but only on 64 nodes versus 504.

Yes. Six instances had spawn and build times above the threshold. The worst was a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2, which took 50.72 seconds to spawn against a median of 19.74 seconds (ratio 2.57). The slow VMs are nova-compute lines, five of them clustered on 2017-05-14 between about 21:08 and 21:47.
Scope: openstack dataset, whole corpus for the outlier scan (baseline = each pattern over the whole dataset; threshold = max(median + 6×MAD, median + 2 s)); results not truncated. The search of 2017-05-14 21:00:00 → 22:00:00 was truncated to 10 of 80 log lines. The context pull covers instance a445709b, 2017-05-14 21:41:33 → 21:45:33.
Normal spawn time (pattern 'Took <N> seconds to spawn the instance on the hypervisor', n=2066) has median 19.74 s, p95 21.008 s and threshold 22.26 s. Normal build time (n=2066) has median 20.55 s and threshold 23.07 s. 6 log lines were flagged for each of the two patterns.
The outlier scan returned 16 flagged log lines in total across 6 flagged instances. Twelve of these are the spawn and build lines of the 6 instances (2 each); the other 4 are metadata/API request lines.
Slowest instance a445709b-6ad0-40ec-8860-bec60b6ca0c2 at 2017-05-14 21:43:33.762: 'Took 50.72 seconds to spawn the instance on the hypervisor.' (ratio 2.57 vs median 19.74) and 'Took 51.59 seconds to build instance.' (ratio 2.51 vs median 20.55).
Instance 544fd51c-4edc-4780-baae-ba1d80a0acfc spawned in 41.81 s (ratio 2.12), build 42.81 s, first seen 2017-05-14 21:08:19.736. Instance 1643649d-2f42-4303-bfcd-7798baec19f9 spawned in 31.27 s (ratio 1.58), build 32.12 s, at 2017-05-14 21:47:20.593.
Instance ae651dff-c7ad-43d6-ac96-bbcd820ccca8 spawned in 29.46 s (ratio 1.49), build 30.32 s, at 2017-05-14 21:09:11.081. Instance d7d68893-c44f-4e7c-8d4b-0e7801d62776 spawned in 26.69 s (ratio 1.35), build 27.61 s, at 2017-05-14 21:45:04.509.
Instance f0ff0b46-b3cd-43e6-97eb-839fd1cdaa87 spawned in 22.56 s (ratio 1.14), build 23.34 s, at 2017-05-16 16:49:11.697. This is only just over the threshold, and it is the only flagged instance outside 2017-05-14.
Timeline for a445709b: 21:42:42.360 'Claim successful'; 21:42:43.044 'Creating image'; 21:43:27.498 'VM Started (Lifecycle Event)'; 21:43:27.561 'VM Paused (Lifecycle Event)'; 21:43:33.752 'VM Resumed (Lifecycle Event)'; 21:43:33.761 'Instance spawned successfully.'; 21:43:33.762 'Took 50.72 seconds to spawn the instance on the hypervisor.'

sql: WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, coalesce(latency_ms / 1000.0, CAST(nullif(regexp_extract(body, 'Took ([\d.]+) seconds', 1), '') AS DOUBLE)) AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM patterns WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND (strpos(template, 'Took <N> seconds') > 0 OR strpos(template, ' time: <N>') > 0))) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.instance_id, l.request_id, coalesce(l.latency_ms / 1000.0, CAST(nullif(regexp_extract(l.body, 'Took ([\d.]+) seconds', 1), '') AS DOUBLE)) AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT f.line_id, f.ts, f.pattern_id, f.instance_id, f.request_id, round(f.value_s, 3) AS value_s, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(f.value_s / t.med, 2) AS ratio, f.body FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold ORDER BY ratio DESC, f.ts LIMIT 30

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, coalesce(latency_ms / 1000.0, CAST(nullif(regexp_extract(body, 'Took ([\d.]+) seconds', 1), '') AS DOUBLE)) AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM patterns WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND (strpos(template, 'Took <N> seconds') > 0 OR strpos(template, ' time: <N>') > 0))) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.instance_id, l.request_id, coalesce(l.latency_ms / 1000.0, CAST(nullif(regexp_extract(l.body, 'Took ([\d.]+) seconds', 1), '') AS DOUBLE)) AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT t.pattern_id, p.template, t.n, round(t.med, 3) AS median_s, round(t.p95, 3) AS p95_s, round(t.mad, 3) AS mad_s, round(t.threshold, 3) AS threshold_s, count(*) FILTER (WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold) AS flagged FROM t JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'openstack' AND p.pattern_id = t.pattern_id LEFT JOIN f ON f.pattern_id = t.pattern_id GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY flagged DESC, t.n DESC

WITH b AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS n, median(v) AS med, mad(v) AS mad, quantile_cont(v, 0.95) AS p95 FROM (SELECT pattern_id, coalesce(latency_ms / 1000.0, CAST(nullif(regexp_extract(body, 'Took ([\d.]+) seconds', 1), '') AS DOUBLE)) AS v FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM patterns WHERE dataset = 'openstack' AND (strpos(template, 'Took <N> seconds') > 0 OR strpos(template, ' time: <N>') > 0))) WHERE v IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), t AS (SELECT *, greatest(med + 6.0 * mad, med + 2.0) AS threshold FROM b ), f AS ( SELECT l.line_id, l.ts, l.pattern_id, l.instance_id, l.request_id, coalesce(l.latency_ms / 1000.0, CAST(nullif(regexp_extract(l.body, 'Took ([\d.]+) seconds', 1), '') AS DOUBLE)) AS value_s, l.body FROM logs l WHERE l.dataset = 'openstack' AND l.pattern_id IN (SELECT pattern_id FROM t) ) SELECT f.instance_id, max(round(f.value_s / t.med, 2)) AS max_ratio, count(*) AS flagged_lines, min(f.ts) AS first_ts FROM f JOIN t USING (pattern_id) WHERE f.value_s > t.threshold AND f.instance_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 50

Two FATAL KERNEL "kernel panic" log lines (pattern_id 576) hit R43-M0 within a fraction of a second of each other at 2005-08-19 13:56:00, on nodes R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 and R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11. Rack R43 has no other log lines in the hour before, and the next R43-M0 line is a ciod LOGIN failure at 2005-08-19 17:12:37.933881.
Scope: bgl (BG/L); midplane R43-M0, mainly 2005-08-19 13:30 → 14:30, with context from 2005-08-18 00:00 → 2005-08-21 00:00 and rack R43 ±1 h around the first panic. The "kernel panic" corpus search was not truncated.
In 2005-08-19 13:30 → 14:30, R43-M0 has 2 log lines on 2 distinct nodes, first 2005-08-19 13:56:00.280831 and last 2005-08-19 13:56:00.628434. Both are KERNEL, FATAL, pattern_id 576, body "kernel panic": R43-M0-NC-I:J18-U01 (line_id 3069219) and R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11 (line_id 3069220).
Within 1 hour either side of line 3069219, rack R43 has before_total 0 and after_total 1; the single following line is the second kernel panic (line 3069220). The panic is local to 2 nodes of R43-M0, with no neighbouring lines in rack R43 in that window.
Before the panic, the last R43-M0 lines are ciod errors on 2005-08-19 12:24:59 → 12:26:12, ahead of the 13:56:00 panic: "ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory" (pattern_id 586, e.g. line 3068403 on R43-M0-N4-I:J18-U11) and "ciod: Error reading message prefix after LOGIN_MESSAGE on CioStream socket to 172.16.96.116:40777: Link has been severed" (pattern_id 435, line 3069072 on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11). All are FATAL.
After the panic, the next R43-M0 line is at 2005-08-19 17:12:37.933881 on R43-M0-N8-I:J18-U11: "ciod: LOGIN chdir(/home/auselton/testing) failed: No such file or directory". Further LOGIN chdir failures and one "Link has been severed" line follow on the same nodes up to 17:12:45.728405.
Earlier on R43-M0, FATAL KERNEL lines "rts: kernel terminated for reason 1001" (and one with reason 1004) appeared from 2005-08-18 00:55:55.828459 (pattern_id 562). INFO lines "ciod: generated 64 core files for program /bgl/apps/swl-prep/ibm-swl/functional/sppm_chkpt/run/sppm" appeared from 2005-08-18 12:40:17.079286 (pattern_id 584).
Rate vs usual: in 2005-08-19 13:00 → 15:00, R43-M0 had window_lines 2 (1.0 per hour), against a baseline of 391 lines over 84 windows (2.327 per hour, ratio 0.4, baseline_max_per_window 176). The panic is not a volume burst for this midplane.
Across the corpus, "kernel panic" matches 18 log lines on 18 distinct nodes, first 2005-08-15 16:31:53.274944 and last 2005-11-11 13:51:11.907657. The only R43-M0 panics are the 2 lines at 2005-08-19 13:56:00. The earlier ones are on other racks (R04-M0, R24-M1, R10-M0 on 2005-08-15), so the pattern recurs across the machine, but this is the first on R43-M0.
Hypothesis: Possibly the panics are linked to the preceding job-launch trouble on R43-M0 (ciod LOGIN chdir failures and severed CioStream links from 12:24:59 → 12:26:12). A node-level kernel fault could be triggered by, or coincide with, that job's I/O-node state. The same LOGIN failures reappear at 17:12:37.933881, so this is not established. Would confirm: Check whether the job or user behind /home/auselton/testing was running on R43-M0-NC and R43-M0-N8 at 13:56. Check the I/O-node (J18) console or RAS logs around 13:56:00 for the panic cause. Check whether the other kernel-panic nodes had similar ciod errors in the preceding hours.
Unknown: The root cause of the kernel panic is not in these logs; the body is only "kernel panic" with no stack or reason code.

Unknown: Whether the 2 affected nodes rebooted or how long they were unavailable is not shown; no recovery lines appear until the ciod errors at 17:12:37.933881.
Unknown: Job impact, downtime and customer impact are not in the logs.

Also compare the hours before the other "kernel panic" nodes to see whether ciod LOGIN or link-severed errors precede them. — The panic line carries no cause, and the ciod failures from 12:24:59 → 12:26:12 are the only nearby signal in the data.

The top three priorities are all KERNEL hardware-fault patterns owned by node-platform: external DDR uncorrectable error, EDRAM bank uncorrectable error, and machine check interrupt. Each recurred about twice as often as in the prior period. The decision is whether node-platform gets a focused hardware review of these memory and machine-check faults.
Scope: Datasets bgl and openstack, 2005-10-01 to 2005-11-01, compared with 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01. Filter: problem patterns only (jev). For bgl, 84 candidates matched and only the top 10 are shown, so results are truncated. The openstack query returned no results.
Team roll-up for node-platform: 43 problem patterns, 251 bursts versus 217 in the previous period (change 34), and 4150 log lines.
Team roll-up for hpc-workloads: 33 problem patterns, 43 bursts versus 18 in the previous period (change 25), and 36295 log lines.
Team roll-up for cluster-control: 8 problem patterns, 30 bursts versus 32 in the previous period (change -2), and 1213 log lines.
The openstack dataset returned 0 problem-pattern matches for this period.
The pattern 'Kill job <N> timed out. Block freed.' (node-platform) has the largest growth: 44 bursts versus 29 in the previous period (change 15), active in 6 weeks. It ranks 5th by score at 75.4.
1. Uncorrectable error detected in external DDR (hardware failure judgment) — owner node-platform — Score 82.4; 4 bursts versus 2 in the previous period (change 2); 4 nodes; active in 4 weeks. — Decide whether to fund a hardware review of the affected memory on these nodes.
2. Uncorrectable error detected in EDRAM bank (hardware failure judgment) — owner node-platform — Score 82.0; 4 bursts versus 2 in the previous period (change 2); 4 nodes; active in 4 weeks. — Review together with rank 1, since both show the same burst, node and week counts.
3. Machine check interrupt: L<N> major internal error (hardware failure judgment) — owner node-platform — Score 80.5; 10 bursts versus 5 in the previous period (change 5); 8 nodes; active in 5 weeks. — Decide on a node-level diagnostic. This pattern has the widest spread of the top three.
Hypothesis: The memory and machine-check patterns may share one underlying hardware fault, since they have identical burst counts and a similar spread across nodes. Would confirm: Check whether the same nodes or hardware locations appear across patterns 124, 122 and 93, and whether hardware diagnostics show faults there.
Unknown: Cost, downtime and customer impact are not in these logs.
Unknown: Root cause is not established by these logs.
Unknown: Only the top 10 of 84 bgl candidates are shown, so lower-ranked patterns were not reviewed.
Next step: Ask node-platform to assign an owner for a hardware review of the top three patterns and report back on affected nodes. — All top three priorities are owned by node-platform, and each had more bursts than in the previous period.
Next step: Request a short assessment of the 'Kill job timed out' pattern, which has the largest growth. — It grew by 15 bursts, from 29 to 44, though its node count is 0 in the results.
Next step: Ask hpc-workloads to review its growth. — Its bursts rose from 18 to 43, with 36295 log lines.

sql: WITH now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS lines, count(DISTINCT node) AS nodes, count(DISTINCT date_trunc('week', ts)) AS weeks_active, count(*) FILTER (WHERE (severity IN ('FATAL', 'FAILURE', 'SEVERE', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL') OR status >= 500)) AS problem_lines FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND pattern_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ), top_node AS ( SELECT pattern_id, max(n) AS top_node_lines FROM ( SELECT pattern_id, node, count(*) AS n FROM logs WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' AND node IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2) GROUP BY 1 ), b_now AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-11-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), b_prev AS ( SELECT pattern_id, count(*) AS bursts_prev FROM bursts WHERE dataset = 'bgl' AND start_ts >= '2005-08-31 00:00:00' AND start_ts < '2005-10-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1 ), base AS ( SELECT p.pattern_id, p.template, p.component, coalesce(o.team, 'unowned') AS team, p.severity, now.lines, now.problem_lines, now.nodes, now.weeks_active, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) AS bursts, coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS bursts_prev, coalesce(b_now.bursts, 0) - coalesce(b_prev.bursts_prev, 0) AS change, round(top_node.top_node_lines::DOUBLE / now.lines, 3) AS top_node_share, p.first_ts AS first_seen, p.first_ts >= '2005-10-01 00:00:00' AS new, round(j.p_fault, 3) AS p_fault, round(j.p_dump, 3) AS p_dump, round(j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump), 3) AS p_problem, j.kind FROM now JOIN patterns p ON p.dataset = 'bgl' AND p.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN pattern_judgments j ON j.dataset = 'bgl' AND j.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN ownership o ON o.dataset = 'bgl' AND o.component = p.component LEFT JOIN top_node ON top_node.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_now ON b_now.pattern_id = now.pattern_id LEFT JOIN b_prev ON b_prev.pattern_id = now.pattern_id WHERE TRUE AND now.problem_lines > 0 AND j.p_fault * (1 - j.p_dump) >= 0.5 ), inputs AS ( SELECT *, round(weeks_active::DOUBLE / 6, 3) AS persistence, round(problem_lines::DOUBLE / lines, 3) AS problem_share, p_problem AS severity_input FROM base ), ranked AS ( SELECT *, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY bursts) AS pr_frequency, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY change) AS pr_trend, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY nodes) AS pr_spread, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY persistence) AS pr_persistence, cume_dist() OVER (ORDER BY severity_input) AS pr_severity FROM inputs ) SELECT *, round(100 * (0.3 * pr_frequency + 0.2 * pr_trend + 0.25 * pr_spread + 0.15 * pr_persistence + 0.1 * pr_severity), 1) AS score FROM ranked ORDER BY score DESC, bursts DESC, pattern_id

Between 2005-10-01 and 2005-11-01, log lines matching "machine check interrupt" ran 21 in the week of 2005-10-03, then 11, 11 and 11 in the next three weeks; the first (4 lines) and last (3 lines) buckets cover only part of a week. The problem is owned by node-platform (61 of 61 matching log lines).
Scope: Dataset bgl, 2005-10-01 00:00:00 to 2005-11-01 00:00:00 (burst change compares against 2005-08-31 to 2005-10-01). Phrase search "machine check interrupt", weekly buckets, unit = log lines. Trend and ownership results were not truncated. The pattern ranking returned 50 of 152 problem patterns (truncated), but the three machine-check-interrupt patterns are all in it. The sample search returned only 3 example lines.
The phrase "machine check interrupt" matched 61 log lines in the period, first at 2005-10-01 11:02:23.732541 and last at 2005-10-31 20:43:30.119580.
Weekly log lines by bucket start: 2005-09-26 had 4, 2005-10-03 had 21, 2005-10-10 had 11, 2005-10-17 had 11, 2005-10-24 had 11, 2005-10-31 had 3.
All 61 matching log lines belong to one team, node-platform (groups_total 1).
The matching log lines came from 54 distinct nodes; the sampled lines are severity FATAL, component KERNEL.
Pattern 33 'machine check interrupt': 37 log lines, 34 nodes, 6 weeks active, 34 bursts versus 38 in the previous period (change -4).
Pattern 86 'machine check interrupt (bit=<N>d): L<N> dcache unit data parity error': 14 log lines, 13 nodes, 5 weeks active, 14 bursts versus 14 previously (change 0).
Pattern 93 'machine check interrupt (bit=<N>): L<N> major internal error': 10 log lines, 8 nodes, 5 weeks active, 10 bursts versus 5 previously (change 5).
1. Plain 'machine check interrupt' FATAL kernel messages (pattern 33), the largest recurring variant.
